assumptions: THIS INCREMENT IS THE SECOND HALF OF #131: the fixtures and the auth-context helper leave the --command argv path for stdin, as migrations did. It is loader plumbing in scripts/db/** and one contract-test rule; it adds no migration, grant, policy or case.

A FIXTURE IS ONE TRANSACTION BY ITS OWN TEXT and the helper install is a set of CREATE OR REPLACE statements, so the stdin path for them is feed() -- no begin/commit wrapping -- and not script(), which wraps. Reusing script() would nest a transaction inside one.

ON STDIN A LINE BEGINNING WITH A BACKSLASH IS A META-COMMAND PSQL EXECUTES (measured: `\! echo PWNED` ran and returned rows). The static rule that held migrations to carrying none now holds every fixture and the helper. Cases keep --command and are not held to it.

THE OLD CEILING IS LINUX MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131,072), where CI runs; macOS has no per-argument cap and a 141,425-byte script passed through --command on this machine. The evidence records that and does not claim a local refusal.

security_privacy_cost_impact: No grant, policy, role or read surface changes. The one door stdin opens -- a backslash line psql executes as a shell command -- is closed by a static rule over every file the loader feeds, measured open (§2) before the rule was relied on. The fixtures are repository files read by a reviewer; the rule is defence against a fixture that arrives with one by mistake, not against an adversary who can already edit the repository.
migration_and_data_impact: None. No migration; the loader feeds the same eleven fixtures and the same helper, as written, and the same 845 cases pass.
compatibility_impact: scripts/db/psql-driver.mjs gains feed(); script() and query() are unchanged. Any caller that loaded a fixture through query() would still work under the old ceiling; the loader is the only caller and it moved.
known_limitations: Cases still run under --command by design; a case over 131,072 bytes would meet the ceiling on Linux. None is within two orders of magnitude of it.
The static rule reads the first non-blank character of each line; a meta-command after a statement on the same line is not psql syntax and is not what the rule guards.
open_risks_or_blockers: None opened. The second-pass record §5 item "fixture loads still go through --command" is paid by this increment.
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert the merge commit: the loader returns to query() for fixtures and the helper, feed() goes, and the rule goes with it. Nothing in the database depends on which path loaded a fixture.
recommended_next_work_packages: Batch 102 (updated_by at INSERT is the caller, thirteen tables), prepared on its own branch and next in this queue.
The pre-080 families closures once the Owner picks a row of the S8 map (a0-pre-080-families-s8-map-2026-09-15.md).
reviewer_instructions: Read feed() beside script() in scripts/db/psql-driver.mjs and confirm the one difference is the wrapping, and why.

Put a line `\! echo x` into any fixture and run the contract suite: the rule must name the file and line. Then run rls-smoke on a scratch database with the same line: psql executes it -- that is the door the rule closes.
